proof:
# Valid additive midpoint and integer-chord certificates

Let n>=1,d>=1, let C be compact and convex in R^n x R^d, and put S=C intersect (Z^n x R^d). Assume the mixed d-volume M=sum_z vol_d(C_z) is positive. All sums below are over distinct integer fibers and therefore add without overlap. Let gamma=gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d.

## Lemma 1: midpoint certificate

Let u,v be distinct integer points of the same parity, put m=(u+v)/2, and assume K_u=C_u and K_v=C_v have positive d-volumes a,b. Let c_u,c_v be their ordinary centroids and put c=(c_u+c_v)/2. Then y=(m,c) belongs to S and

depth_S(y)>= gamma/M * ( [ (a^{1/d}+b^{1/d})/2 ]^d + min(a,b) ).

Proof. Convexity puts (K_u+K_v)/2 inside C_m, and c lies in this Minkowski sum. Thus y belongs to S. It suffices to treat a halfspace whose boundary passes through y, because any containing closed halfspace can be translated inward until its boundary passes through y, only decreasing its intersection with S.

Write such a halfspace as

H={ (z,x): alpha dot (z-m)+beta dot (x-c)>=0 }.

If beta is nonzero, let A={x in K_u:beta dot(x-c_u)>=0} and B={x in K_v:beta dot(x-c_v)>=0}. Ordinary Gruenbaum gives vol(A)>=gamma a and vol(B)>=gamma b. If beta=0, use A=K_u and B=K_v; the same inequalities remain true. Every point in (A+B)/2 belongs to C_m and satisfies the halfspace inequality. By Brunn-Minkowski,

vol_d(C_m intersect H_m)
>=vol_d((A+B)/2)
>=[(vol(A)^{1/d}+vol(B)^{1/d})/2]^d
>=gamma[(a^{1/d}+b^{1/d})/2]^d.

The signed halfspace values at (u,c_u) and (v,c_v) sum to zero. At least one of these two points belongs to H. The cut in that endpoint fiber contains its centroid, so its volume is at least gamma a or gamma b respectively, and in either case is at least gamma min(a,b). The endpoint fiber and the midpoint fiber are distinct, so their contributions add. Dividing by M proves the result. The case beta=0 is included; closed boundaries are retained throughout.

No assertion that c is the centroid of the Minkowski sum is used or needed.

## Lemma 2: integer-chord certificate

Let u,v be distinct integer points with positive-volume fibers of volumes a,b and centroids c_u,c_v. Suppose L is a positive integer such that

z_j=u+(j/L)(v-u) is integer for j=0,...,L.

Set t_j=j/L,

c_j=(1-t_j)c_u+t_j c_v,
w_j=[(1-t_j)a^{1/d}+t_j b^{1/d}]^d.

Then y_j=(z_j,c_j) belongs to S, and for every i in {0,...,L},

depth_S(y_i)>=gamma/M * min( sum_{j=0}^i w_j, sum_{j=i}^L w_j ).

Proof. Convexity gives (1-t_j)K_u+t_jK_v subset C_{z_j}, so y_j belongs to S. Fix an ambient halfspace H containing y_i, and form A,B as in Lemma 1 using its continuous normal beta. The signed halfspace value at y_j is affine in j. Therefore the set of indices j whose y_j belongs to H is a prefix, a suffix, or all indices, and it contains i. Its total w_j weight is consequently at least the stated minimum.

For every such captured index j, the Minkowski sum (1-t_j)A+t_jB lies in C_{z_j} intersect H_{z_j}: its signed value is the nonnegative value at y_j plus a nonnegative weighted sum of the centered continuous normal values. Brunn-Minkowski gives its volume at least gamma w_j. Summing these bounds over distinct captured integer fibers proves the claim.

For d=0 all nonempty fibers are single points, the centroid is that point, and the corresponding chord weights are one. Convexity supplies the intermediate points, and the same prefix/suffix argument proves the counting-measure analogue directly, without using a 1/d exponent.

## Corollary 3: three collinear fibers with equal endpoint volumes

Suppose n=1 and exactly three positive-volume integer fibers occur at consecutive positions u,u+1,u+2. Let the two endpoint volumes equal a>0 and let the middle volume be b. Then OC holds, without any hypothesis on the shapes or centroids of the three fibers.

The midpoint certificate gives a point of unnormalized depth at least 2gamma a. The centroid of the middle fiber gives a point of unnormalized depth at least gamma b. Since

max(2a,b)>=(2a+b)/2=M/2,

one of these two actual points has normalized depth at least gamma/2. Equivalently, if b>=2a use its centroid, and if b<=2a use the averaged endpoint centroids. Equality b=2a is covered by either choice.

If some other nonempty integer fibers have zero d-volume, they do not alter M or these certificates. To describe exactly three nonempty fibers instead, the assertion is an immediate special case.

## Lemma 4: a safe binary certificate construction

For a compact convex d-dimensional body D and a point c in D, say k is a certified capacity if every closed continuous halfspace containing c cuts from D volume at least k. Suppose two nodes have bodies D_1 subset C_{z_1}, D_2 subset C_{z_2}, points c_1,c_2, and capacities k_1,k_2. If z=(z_1+z_2)/2 is integer, then

D=(D_1+D_2)/2 subset C_z,
c=(c_1+c_2)/2,
k=[(k_1^{1/d}+k_2^{1/d})/2]^d

define a new valid capacity. The proof is the same positive-half Brunn-Minkowski argument, with k_1,k_2 in place of gamma a,gamma b.

Now build a finite binary tree of these nodes, requiring all node fiber labels to be distinct. At a centroid leaf with actual fiber volume a, take k=gamma a. Define numbers b at the leaves by b=k, and at every internal node by

b=k+min(b_left,b_right).

Then every ambient halfspace containing the root point cuts volume at least b_root from the union of the actual fibers labeling this tree, and hence from S. Prove this stronger union-of-subtree assertion by induction. The halfspace contains at least one child point because the root point is their midpoint. Apply the child's certificate within that child's subtree and add the root-fiber capacity. The distinct-label hypothesis guarantees that the newly added root fiber does not overlap any fiber counted by the child certificate. This proves the induction step and the bound.

This is only a valid certificate construction. No claim that a sufficiently strong tree always exists is made. If labels repeat, or if capacities from both children are added simultaneously, additional disjointness proofs are required.
